newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-ITALY MUST BEAT CANADA FOR PLACE IN FINALS.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-ITALY MUST BEAT CANADA FOR PLACE IN FINALS.

text.p: Italy drew 2-2 with Norway at the ice hockey world championship on Friday to set up a showdown with Canada for a place in the medal round.
The stalemate left Italy fourth in pool B with three points, two behind Canada.
They clash on Saturday in their final round-robin match. Italy must win to qualify but Canada go through with a draw.
The top three in each pool proceed to the final round while the bottom three move to Tampere and the relegation tournament.
Sweden and the United States head the pool on six points.
Norway almost ended Italy's hopes when they struck twice in the final two minutes.
Ole Elkild Dahlstrom pulled Norway to within one when he swung around the net and beat Italian goalkeeper David Delfino high to the glove side.
Atle Alexander Olsen levelled 49 seconds later when he drifted a low shot from the blue line past a shaken Delphino.
Until then Italy had been in complete control, jumping 2-0 ahead with a pair of first period powerplay goals by Bruno Zarrillo and Bob Nardella.
"We're tired and Canada is a physical team but obviously I believe we still have a chance," said Italian coach Brian Lefley.
"We never really did feel that we had Norway. We felt we should be better able to protect the lead and we weren't able to, so we regard it as a point lost."
